featured_reviews.review_text:
Masoom is a not for profit organization that works with the night school students to work on the academics and provide better career opportunities to them. Masoom began with informal research on the educational problem of night schools culminated in a action program in 2008. Masoom is the first organization in Maharashtra to run a comprehensive “School Transformation Programme” for night school education. Masoom started with 2 night schools in the first year and then gradually increased its spread to 47 schools and 3500 students in the year 2015. Masoom plans to reach out to 210 night schools by 2020 impacting 20,000 night school students in Maharashtra.

The ‘Night School Transformation Program’ is specifically tailored to meet the needs of the night school and the individual students who are mainly school dropouts from poor socio-economic background, most of them working during the day and supporting their families.. featured_reviews.name: Farzana Yasmin
featured_reviews.review_text:
Since childhood, I have been visiting Mahim Dargah with my family for ziyarat and returning thereafter. However, I have always observed certain practices taking place there that deeply concern me from an Islamic perspective.

There are women who appear to act possessed, often chained, and people are encouraged to believe in these displays. Many visitors are seen making dua to the Baba buried there, instead of making dua to Allah for him. Such acts go against the teachings of the Qur’an and the Sunnah, which clearly prohibit associating partners with Allah or seeking help from anyone other than Him.

Allah ﷻ says in the Qur’an:

> "And that the masjids are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone along with Allah."
(Surah Al-Jinn, 72:18)

And in another verse:

> "Do not call upon anyone besides Allah; such a one can neither benefit you nor harm you."
(Surah Yunus, 10:106)

Our beloved Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said:

> "When you ask, ask Allah; and when you seek help, seek help from Allah."
(Jami` at-Tirmidhi 2516)

Recently, my mother, who is a patient and cannot sit with her legs folded, had to straighten her leg for comfort. Some individuals objected, saying that she should not keep her leg straight as the maqam (resting place) of the Baba and his companions is nearby. However, Islam teaches us only to show such respect toward the Qibla, not graves.

These practices—bowing, seeking favors, or believing others have divine power—are not part of Islam. Instead, they contradict the pure message of Tawheed (Oneness of Allah) that the Qur’an and Prophet Muhammad ﷺ emphasized.

May Allah guide us all to the right path and protect us from shirk and bid’ah (innovations in religion).
Ameen.

featured_reviews.name: Yasin Khatri
featured_reviews.review_text:
The most noteworthy abode of place at Mahim is the Dargah of Hazrat Makhdoom Shah Baba Mahimi (R.A.). Mahim is one of the most famous area of the city (Mumbai).The Dargah stands on the western side of the Cadel Road and the main enterance faces the east. The dargah is constructed with stone and plaster coated with cement plastering. To the east of it is a two storeyed Nagarkhana or a drum chamber with four arches on the ground floor, for roof of which is surrounded by a green flag. To the north of the tomb is the mosque.
Outside the Dargah premises road, there are flowers shops, Bhatyar Khana (Small hotels) for poor people. For all the 24 hours poor people sit outside the Dargaah in the hope that some Devotee of Hazrat Makhdoom Sahib will come and will serve them with food in the name of Hazrat Makhdoom Sahib.
